reason: Closing I-072 and the four flags is correct, and there is nothing to build, so feasibility is trivially fine (no code, runtime or rule exposure). I checked the facts in exp60-x138-trainlab-a.ipynb. In cell 4 the v1284 coordinate refinement is patched in and the int16 cast is removed. In cell 8, add_safe_divisions_postlink runs right after the presafe hook on the same float nodes_by_id. Cell 0 sets SYMMETRY_TAU 0.6, DIVERGE_UM 2.25, MAX 9.0, SISTER_MAX 14.0, EXISTING_CHILD_MAX 10.0 and DC 0.25. Cell 2 defaults REQUIRE_DIVERGENCE and MUTUAL_NN to on. So the premise is false. The recorded rationale has three problems, though. (1) It closes a strawman. The original I-072 (wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_kaggle-intel.json 'divgates-refined') asked to LOOSEN the gates: re-select DIVERGE {1,1.5,2.25,3} x TAU {0.4,0.6,0.8,off} and re-audit reachability, on the grounds that lattice noise made the gates random. It did not ask for a final-coordinate veto. The loosening version is closed by other evidence. x138 already uses float coordinates. CONTEXT l.210 and l.736-758 record the 11-12 Sep official-metric sweeps: tau 0.6 was best and the response monotone; gates open plus a sister floor gave 27-29 FP ('reachable is not recovered'). And R1-R10 forbid gate re-tuning or knob ladders. (2) The GT numbers are not new: CONTEXT l.736-741 already reports divergence rejecting 49.7% and symmetry 37.7% of GT divisions. The comparison of GT with predicted forks is also confounded. Predicted forks have already passed these same gates on presafe coordinates, so a final-coordinate flag only measures linefit drift. The GT base rate cannot tell whether that drift flags FP forks more often than TP forks. 'Not enriched, so TP-hostile' is therefore not shown. The honest reason is that a 30% veto driven by smoothing drift has no FP-specific mechanism and could only be calibrated in the in-sample lab, which over-trusts (edge filter: +0.016 local, 0 on LB). (3) The young-parent GT rate of 21% is an artefact of sparse annotation, like the stub rate the finding already discounts, so 'closed on GT evidence' is the wrong reason there too. It should be closed as unmotivated: in the dense prediction a young track is fragmentation and hits TP and FP alike, and the dose is 9%. Refractory (1% dose) and div3 are fine to close.
